items.title: GTRD 2026: expanded content and resources for deep learning.
items.summary: Journal: Nucleic acids research. Abstract: Gene Transcription Regulation Database (GTRD; https://gtrd.biouml.org/) contains uniformly annotated and processed NGS data related to transcription regulation: ChIP-seq, ChIP-exo, DNase-seq, MNase-seq, ATAC-seq, and RNA-seq. The latest release significantly extends the number of available experiments. All new ChIP-seq data for human transcription factors (TFs) obtained by the Codebook Consortium were processed and annotated; GTRD now covers 85% of all known human TFs. We added new types of information related to transcription regulation: enhancer regions revealed from analysis of CAGE-seq data and single-cell ATAC-seq data. To facilitate the use of GTRD for building deep learning models, we provide direct access to the MySQL database where metadata are stored and have built profiles with single-nucleotide resolution for ChIP-seq and ATAC-seq data.
items.headline: GTRD 2026 expands transcription regulation data for deep learning
items.brief: The Gene Transcription Regulation Database (GTRD) now includes a vastly increased number of uniformly processed NGS datasets related to transcription regulation, covering 85% of known human transcription factors. It integrates ChIP-seq, ATAC-seq, and enhancer data from CAGE-seq and single-cell ATAC-seq, providing single-nucleotide resolution profiles and direct MySQL access to metadata. This resource facilitates building and training deep learning models for regulatory element prediction.
items.why: GTRD 2026 offers a comprehensive, high-resolution, and uniformly processed dataset crucial for training and benchmarking deep learning models in genomics and epigenomics, directly supporting computational genomics research.
items.korean: GTRD 2026은 인간 전사인자 데이터를 확장하여 딥러닝 모델 구축에 필수적인 고해상도 전사 조절 정보를 제공합니다.

items.title: CellChain: Benchmarking Cross-Scale Evidence Use for Perturbation Reasoning
items.summary: Recent advances in foundation models and large-scale cellular perturbation datasets have driven growing interest in using LLMs to predict and reason about cellular responses. Biological reasoning in this setting involves relating molecular mechanisms, cellular responses, and functional outcomes across scales. Evaluating foundation models therefore requires assessing not only whether their predictions are correct, but also how those predictions depend on the biological evidence provided. We introduce CellChain, an experimentally grounded benchmark comprising 590 biological cases and 2,360 matched evidence-condition instances across gene-dependency prediction, cytokine-axis identification, and drug-sensitivity ranking. CellChain links perturbation experiments and external biological resources through a provenance-aware evidence graph spanning molecular, pathway, transcriptional, and phenotypic information. Task-specific conditions vary evidence coverage, composition, or assignment while preserving questions, candidate answers, reference targets, and scoring rules. Across 18 foundation models, the highest accuracies under prespecified target-evidence conditions are 57.5%, 75.5%, and 70.8%, respectively, and broader evidence coverage does not consistently improve accuracy. On the drug-sensitivity benchmark cohort, matched reference histories outperform swapped histories by an average of 13.0 percentage points in cluster-weighted accuracy. Decision-transition analysis separates corrections, newly introduced errors, and wrong-answer switches, revealing substantial answer changes hidden by small net accuracy differences. CellChain provides controlled comparisons for attributing changes in model predictions to prespecified expansions of biological context, including changes in evidence coverage, composition, and biological assignment.
items.headline: CellChain benchmark evaluates LLMs on multi-scale cellular perturbation reasoning
items.brief: CellChain is a benchmark comprising 590 biological cases and 2,360 evidence-condition instances linking molecular, pathway, transcriptional, and phenotypic data to assess foundation models' ability to reason about cellular perturbations across scales. It tests how model predictions depend on biological evidence composition and coverage, enabling evaluation of multi-scale biological reasoning and evidence integration in LLMs.
items.why: CellChain advances evaluation of biological foundation models by rigorously testing their multi-scale reasoning capabilities and evidence use, directly relevant for computational genomics and biological foundation model development.
items.korean: CellChain은 세포 교란에 대한 다중 규모 추론 능력을 평가하는 생물학적 파운데이션 모델 벤치마크입니다.
items.evidence_note: Preprint status; interpret results with caution.

items.title: A Training-Free Socket for DNA in Frozen Language Models
items.summary: Connecting a DNA foundation model to a large language model (LLM) usually requires training a connector, and often the LLM too. We show that a closed-form map is enough for gene-level questions. Our method, the socket, fits one ridge regression (the plug) from frozen Evo 2 features to the host LLM's own representation of the gene's symbol, name, and description at an early layer. The plug's output replaces the hidden state at placeholder positions, and no gradient passes through the host. We test it on GeneHop, a five-way multiple-choice benchmark split by homology. In a single run on the held-out test set, under a frozen analysis plan, real DNA beats shuffled DNA on all four hosts: by +22.2 points [19.8, 25.0] on Qwen3.5-4B, +26.1 [24.3, 27.9] on Qwen3.6-27B, +16.7 [14.2, 19.7] on Mistral-7B, and +18.4 [16.2, 21.0] on OLMo-2-7B. All four survive Holm correction, every null control stays within two points of the sham level, and the development results agree within 2.3 points. A layer rule that uses no task items was selected on three hosts; it predicted the working layer of the fourth before any DNA-plug scoring on it. A text-only linear map lets one plug feed any other host, at a cost of at most 0.9 points on test. The socket conveys gene identity: nearest-neighbour retrieval recovers 72-84% of the effect, but the plug beats it on every host by 3.0-5.2 points and keeps most of its effect without training homologs.
items.headline: Training-free DNA socket enables gene-level queries in frozen language models
items.brief: The socket method maps DNA foundation model features to large language model (LLM) representations via a single ridge regression plug, enabling gene-level question answering without retraining the LLM or connector. Tested on the GeneHop benchmark, this approach significantly outperforms shuffled DNA baselines across multiple LLM hosts, demonstrating that frozen LLMs can interpret DNA features through a learned linear mapping.
items.why: This method provides an efficient, training-free approach to integrate DNA foundation models with LLMs for gene-level tasks, advancing biological foundation model interoperability.
items.korean: 소켓 방법은 훈련 없이 DNA 모델과 LLM을 연결해 유전자 수준 질문에 답할 수 있게 합니다.

items.title: Limbic circuit alterations in bipolar disorder.
items.summary: Journal: Dialogues in clinical neuroscience. Abstract: INTRODUCTION: This study investigated the spatial and temporal pattern of brain white matter (WM) alterations and their relationship with intrinsic brain activity in bipolar disorder (BD). METHODS: Multimodal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data were collected from 67 BD patients (during manic, depressive, or euthymic phases) and 125 healthy controls (HC) at baseline, and from a subsample of 33 BD patients (in a different illness phase) and 23 HC after follow-up. Analyses of diffusion MRI and resting-state functional MRI were performed to characterise fixel-based metrics in WM and their relationship with intrinsic brain activity in BD and HC, as well as across timepoints. RESULTS: BD exhibited a spatial pattern of WM alterations characterised by reductions in fibre density and/or bundle cross-section involving fornix and cingulum (major limbic pathways), alongside portions of other tracts, compared with HC. Reduced fibre density in the fornix was associated with intrinsic activity changes involving midbrain, thalamus, and connected fronto-temporal cortical areas within the default-mode network in BD. These alterations showed no significant changes over time or across illness phases. CONCLUSIONS: These findings converge on limbic circuit alterations and suggest a relationship between structural abnormalities of the fornix and functional changes in intrinsic brain architecture in BD.
items.headline: Limbic white matter alterations linked to intrinsic brain activity in bipolar disorder
items.brief: Using diffusion and resting-state fMRI in bipolar disorder (BD) patients and controls, reductions in fiber density and bundle cross-section were found in limbic white matter tracts including the fornix and cingulum. Reduced fornix fiber density correlated with altered intrinsic activity in midbrain and thalamus regions. These findings reveal spatial-temporal patterns of white matter disruption associated with BD phases and brain activity changes.
items.why: This study links structural white matter changes to functional brain activity in BD, providing insights into neural substrates relevant for computational genomics and neuroscience.
items.korean: 조현병에서 변연계 백질 변화가 뇌 내재 활동과 연관됨을 보여줍니다.

items.title: Predicting IGD treatment outcomes across interventions using a whole-brain functional connectome biomarker.
items.summary: Journal: Dialogues in clinical neuroscience. Abstract: BACKGROUND: Although treatment approaches have been explored in internet gaming disorder (IGD), however, little is known about the specific neural activity that is associated with treatment outcomes. This study aims to establish a treatment-sensitive network that reliably predicts treatment outcomes across different interventions for IGD. METHODS: Resting-state fMRI data were collected from 90 individuals with IGD who received one of three different intervention protocols (mindfulness meditation, approach bias modification, or retrieval-aversive conditioning training). Connectome-based predictive modelling (CPM) was used to build a treatment-sensitive network to predict individual symptom reduction, then validated them on the external dataset. RESULTS: The negative (r = 0.401, p <.001) and combined network (r = 0.480, p <.001) can significantly predict a reduction of addiction severity (baseline minus post-test). Specifically, the negative network was primarily centred on the motor, subcortical, and salience networks. The positive network primarily involved cerebellar-related connections. Incorporating these into a combined model significantly improved predictive accuracy, suggesting that cerebellar-related connectivity may contribute to the prediction of intervention-related clinical improvement. Finally, the treatment-sensitive network was validated in a separate data. CONCLUSIONS: This study established a treatment-sensitive network based on the whole-brain connectome. These findings provide valuable empirical evidence for identifying biomarkers for IGD treatment and advance personalised therapeutic strategies. CLINICAL TRIALS REGISTRATION: The trial protocol was pre-registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (www.chictr.org.cn; ChiCTR2300077831(MM), ChiCTR2300075869(ApBm), ChiCTR2500095444(R-AC), ChiCTR2400090834(SAE)).
items.headline: Functional connectome predicts treatment outcomes across interventions in internet gaming disorder
items.brief: Resting-state fMRI data from 90 individuals with internet gaming disorder undergoing three different interventions were analyzed using connectome-based predictive modeling. Networks centered on motor, subcortical, and salience regions predicted symptom reduction across treatments. This treatment-sensitive network generalized to external datasets, suggesting a neural biomarker for predicting intervention efficacy in IGD.
items.why: Identifying neural predictors of treatment response advances understanding of brain-behavior links and supports computational approaches in neuroscience and psychology.
items.korean: 기능적 연결망이 인터넷 게임 장애 치료 결과를 예측합니다.

items.title: Vacuum correlation measures as CFT partition functions
items.summary: We show that in any $d$-dimensional CFT, the vacuum sandwiched Rényi mutual information (SRMI) of integer order $n$ between two disjoint balls maps to a CFT partition function on a manifold of topology $\#^{n-1}(S^1 \times S^{d-1})$, with moduli fixed by the ball configuration and single-ball modular flow. At $n=2$, it is given by the thermal partition function on $S^{d-1}$, upper-bounding the von Neumann mutual information. For $n>2$, SRMI diverges at finite separation due to a hot-spot limit of the partition function. Explicit CFT evaluations agree well with density matrix computations.
items.headline: Vacuum sandwiched Rényi mutual information as CFT partition functions on complex manifolds
items.brief: In any d-dimensional conformal field theory (CFT), the vacuum sandwiched Rényi mutual information (SRMI) of integer order n between two disjoint balls corresponds to the CFT partition function on a manifold with topology #^{n-1}(S^1 × S^{d-1}), with moduli fixed by the ball configuration. At n=2, it equals the thermal partition function on S^{d-1}, bounding the von Neumann mutual information. For n>2, SRMI diverges at finite separation due to hot-spot limits. Explicit CFT calculations match density matrix computations.
items.why: This work connects entanglement measures in CFTs to partition functions on complex topologies, providing rigorous tools for quantum information and theoretical physics.
items.korean: 진공 샌드위치 Rényi 상호정보가 복잡한 다양체 위의 CFT 분배 함수와 대응됨을 보입니다.
